papers.title: Business model tools as cognitive mediators: sensebreaking and sensemaking in business model innovation
papers.abstract: Purpose Business model innovation represents a central challenge for companies facing technological, competitive and institutional change, requiring incumbent firms to move beyond the taken-for-granted assumptions embedded in their established business models. This article examines how business model tools enable sensebreaking and sensemaking throughout the business model innovation process, investigating how their complementary mobilisation helps organisations construct and develop alternative business models in the context of digital servitisation. Design/methodology/approach The article draws on an interventionist case study conducted over nearly four years in an Italian manufacturer developing smart connected products for industrial machines. The empirical material was collected predominantly through meetings held during the project, semi-structured interviews and document analysis. Findings Using sensebreaking and sensemaking as the theoretical lens, we show how business model innovation unfolds through three interrelated cognitive mechanisms. First, business model tools destabilise incumbent business model assumptions by exposing the limitations of existing product logics. Second, they provide a shared interpretive platform through which alternative service-oriented business models are collectively reframed. Finally, they stabilise these emerging interpretations by translating them into organisational and calculative commitments. Originality/value The article conceptualises a break-then-make process in which sensebreaking opens interpretive space and sensemaking constructs alternative business model logics and translates them into organisational commitments. The study contributes to business model innovation research by shifting attention from business model design to the cognitive mechanisms that enable it.

papers.title: Dynamic platform strategies in an interconnected ecosystem: Navigating standards and complements in the emerging smart home ecosystem
papers.abstract: Whereas prior platform research has mostly assumed standardized interfaces that are platform-specific, we examine how platform strategies based on third-party standards have become prevalent in a nascent ecosystem. Based on a longitudinal analysis of 97 smart home platforms, we analyze the value creation and capture benefits of four platform modes defined by two dimensions: the source of complements (first- or third-party complements) and the standardized interfaces used to connect these complements (first- or third-party standards). Our analysis demonstrates a trend from closed strategies (only first-party complements based on first-party standards) towards strategies that (also) rely on third-party standards. We find that startups and diversifying entrants make different strategic choices at entry and that firms increasingly combine platform modes over time to leverage their distinct value creation and capture benefits. Our findings contribute insights into the ecosystem conditions and pre-entry capabilities of firms under which strategies relying on third-party standards become viable and how this contributes to the proliferation of standards, platforms, and strategies in an ecosystem. We also theorize the time-dependent strategic choices of entrants navigating a nascent ecosystem and the complex complementary and competitive relations that emerge in an ecosystem with interconnected platforms as a result.

papers.title: Using leverage points to identify interventions for transitioning the Dutch road infrastructure sector toward sustainability
papers.abstract: The transition toward sustainability in infrastructure sectors requires interventions that address systemic lock-ins rather than isolated technological improvements. However, innovation ecosystem research offers only limited guidance on how public-sector-driven ecosystems can be intentionally steered toward sustainability under conditions of structural inertia. This study employs Donella Meadows' leverage points framework to identify and categorize potential systemic interventions in the Dutch road infrastructure innovation ecosystem. Using an action-oriented research design conducted over 1.5 years with public clients, contractors, and knowledge institutions, the study identifies 25 interventions across five thematic areas. The findings show that interventions predominantly target system design and feedback structures, the strengthening of governance, foresight, and integration capabilities rather than focusing on parameter-level change. This highlights how transformations in public-sector innovation ecosystems emerge through the gradual reconfiguration of rules, information flows, and coordination mechanisms. The study contributes to innovation ecosystem research by demonstrating how leverage points can be used to guide and structure ecosystem-level intervention strategies and support deliberate steering of public-sector-driven innovation ecosystems toward sustainability.
papers.summary_ja: Donella Meadowsのレバレッジポイント論をオランダの道路インフラ・イノベーション・エコシステムに適用し、公共調達主導のエコシステムを持続可能性へと意図的に転換するための25の介入策を特定した。

papers.title: Mapping urban-industrial symbiosis through a business ecosystem lens
papers.abstract: This paper examines the evolution of urban industrial symbiosis (UIS) through a business ecosystem lens. UIS, defined as the synergistic integration of urban and industrial systems where waste and by-products are repurposed as industrial inputs, has demonstrated strong potential to address climate change, urbanization challenges, and supply chain vulnerabilities. Existing UIS research has primarily focused on material flows, network structures, and policy arrangements. However, limited attention has been given to the entrepreneurial and business dimensions of UIS. This paper bridges these gaps by applying business ecosystem theory to map the roles, relationships, and dynamics within UIS.

papers.title: Creating Digital Sustainable Business Models in Cluster‐Based Energy Ecosystems
papers.abstract: Overlapping economic, social, sustainable, health, and military crises create new spaces for scientific research to be applied to practice. The paper focuses on constructing and configuring digital sustainable business models for energy ecosystems that can effectively respond to and mitigate the impacts of dynamic climate change. This topic is important as it contributes to the global transition toward resilient and resource-efficient energy systems. The research builds on established concepts and advances digital sustainable business model design for cluster-based energy ecosystems.

papers.title: Knowledge protection and modularity of innovation activities in firms: Evidence from US trade secrecy law
papers.abstract: Strategy scholars have theoretically explored the relationship between legal knowledge protection and modularity of innovation activities in firms, but this relationship has yet to be empirically tested in the literature. Leveraging state-level changes in US trade secrecy law and using a network modularity measure, this paper examines how trade secret protection affects the modularity of firms' innovation activities. Analyzing intrafirm inventor collaboration patterns in a sample of US public firms, we find that stronger trade secret protection increases the modularity of firms' innovation networks. This effect is particularly pronounced for firms with higher levels of co-inventor diversity and for those operating in competitive industries.

papers.title: From academic lab to spinoff: How opportunity beliefs evolve from individual to venture during technology-market matching
papers.abstract: Academic labs are central to the creation of radical-generic technologies. Yet translating these inventions into successful innovations poses a significant challenge as academic scientists often struggle to identify and prioritize viable markets in the early stages of commercialization. This study examines how individual scientists' opportunity beliefs evolve into the shared commercialization strategy of an academic spinoff. Using a longitudinal single-case study of the technology-market matching process, we trace how opportunity beliefs are constructed, refined, and institutionalized as scientists transition from lab-based research to venture creation.

papers.title: Design management and research in business strategies and project development
papers.abstract: Design management directly impacts the change in management processes, from the Taylorist administration model, which is hierarchical, to a more flexible model that promotes individual proposals, actions, and risk management. In this article, we present the exploratory research of a Canadian company's business decisions and project processes from the perspective of all departments involved in the same project flow. Based on data collected from interviews with Design Leads, Researchers, Project Owners, Business Analysts, Front-End Developers, Back-End Developers, and System Architects, in this research we identified the process routines and decisions that generate business bottlenecks, as well as possible alternative solutions from the design management perspective.

papers.title: Contemporary and Future Challenges for Structured Democratic Dialogue
papers.abstract: Structured Democratic Dialogue (SDD) is a participatory problem structuring methodology grounded in Structured Dialogic Design Science. It was created to help diverse stakeholders co-construct influence maps that reveal leverage points and support coordinated action. This paper addresses design choices for face-to-face workshops (participant numbers, duration, sequencing of problem/solution analyses), how to handle tangled or circular influence patterns (including time-horizon considerations) and how to integrate feasibility/impact criteria with mapping outputs. It also explores barriers to widespread adoption and outlines a future research agenda.
